name: Erosive pustular dermatosis of the scalp

criteria.description: Presence of chronic erosions and pustules localized to the scalp
Histopathological findings showing sterile pustules with neutrophilic infiltrate and epidermal atrophy
Exclusion of infectious causes by negative bacterial and fungal cultures
History of preceding scalp trauma or actinic damage
Improvement with topical corticosteroids or immunosuppressive therapy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria must be met: chronic scalp erosions and pustules, consistent histopathology, and exclusion of infection
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and histopathological; exclusion of infection is critical.

laboratory: Negative bacterial and fungal cultures from pustules
Mildly elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) in some cases
imaging: Not routinely indicated; scalp ultrasound may show skin thinning
other: Histopathology: sterile pustules with neutrophilic infiltrate, epidermal atrophy, and fibrosis

distinguishingFeatures: Follicular pustules with tufted hair follicles
Positive immunofluorescence for IgG and C3

redFlags: Rapid progression of scalp erosions with systemic symptoms
Failure to respond to topical corticosteroids
Signs of secondary bacterial infection or sepsis
references: Bertolotti A, et al. Erosive pustular dermatosis of the scalp: a review. Dermatol Ther. 2020;33(6):e13903.
Pye RJ, et al. Erosive pustular dermatosis of the scalp: clinical and histopathological features. Br J Dermatol. 1993;129(5):553-559.
